reference: Stress Relief (S5E13 here; a two-part episode, split S5E14-15). Dwight sets a fire on purpose (cigarette into a trash can of paper and lighter fluid, also cuts the phones, blocks/heats doors, sets off firecrackers) as a surprise fire-safety drill, because nobody paid attention to his PowerPoint fire safety talk the week before: 'experience is the best teacher.' It ends with Stanley's heart attack.

evidence.line: Dwight: Last week I gave a fire safety talk. And nobody paid any attention. It's my own fault for using PowerPoint... experience is the best teacher. [lights a cigarette] Today, smoking is gonna save lives. [throws cigarette into garbage can filled with paper and lighter fluid]
Dwight: [blowing air horn] ... This has been a test of our emergency preparedness. There is no fire. It was only a simulation.
David Wallace: You could have burned down the whole building.

caveats: Don't confuse with The Fire (S2E4), where Ryan starts the fire with a cheese pita in the toaster oven, not Dwight. Accept episode by title or split numbering (S5E14/15).
question: In which episode does Dwight start a fire in the office, and why does he do it?
